name: Dulaglutide
route_note: subcutaneous injection once weekly via single-dose pen (0.75–4.5 mg)

discovery.note: Two DPP-4-resistant GLP-1 analogue chains fused through a peptide linker to a modified human IgG4 Fc fragment.

tagline: A weekly GLP-1 agonist built on an antibody Fc backbone
summary: Dulaglutide is a once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist made by fusing GLP-1 analogues to an immunoglobulin Fc fragment, which slows clearance. It lowers glucose and modestly reduces weight, and the REWIND trial showed reduced cardiovascular events in a broad type 2 diabetes population.
mechanism: Each dulaglutide molecule carries two GLP-1 analogue peptides, modified to resist DPP-4, joined to a modified IgG4 Fc domain. The large size limits renal filtration and the Fc region extends half-life to about five days.
Binding to the GLP-1 receptor increases glucose-dependent insulin release, reduces glucagon secretion and slows gastric emptying, with central appetite effects producing modest weight loss.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (adults and children 10 years and older)
Reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with CVD or multiple risk factors

history.title: Approval
history.detail: FDA approves Trulicity in September 2014; EU approval follows in November 2014.

history.title: REWIND
history.detail: REWIND, in 9,901 patients mostly without established CVD, shows a 12% reduction in major cardiovascular events.

history.title: Expansion
history.detail: FDA adds a cardiovascular indication and approves higher 3 mg and 4.5 mg doses.

history.title: AWARD-11
history.detail: AWARD-11 shows the 3.0 and 4.5 mg doses lower HbA1c and weight more than 1.5 mg.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: Trulicity is approved for children aged 10 and over with type 2 diabetes.

safety.boxed_warning: Risk of thyroid C-cell tumours: caused C-cell tumours in rodents; contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

facts: REWIND enrolled a majority of participants without established cardiovascular disease, unlike most GLP-1 outcome trials.
